question: Which of the following demineralises the enamel of the teeth?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Acids produced by bacteria**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acids produced by bacteria** are responsible for demineralising the enamel of the teeth.
 
• These acids are produced when bacteria in the mouth metabolize sugars from food and drink.
 
• The demineralisation process weakens the enamel, making the teeth more susceptible to decay and cavities.
 
• Maintaining good oral hygiene and reducing sugar intake can help prevent the production of these harmful acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Enamel** is the hard, outer surface layer of your teeth that serves to protect against tooth decay.
 
• It is the hardest and most highly mineralized substance in the human body.
 
• Despite its strength, enamel can be eroded by acids and physical wear.
 
• Once enamel is lost, it cannot be regenerated by the body, which is why preventive care is essential.
